analyses.key_findings: On the 5-year dataset (n=8585), supply_contract events show a slightly negative aggregate t5_net mean of -0.11% (PF 0.96) and realistic mean of -0.29%, reversing the Loop-10 2yr positive_noisy +0.39% baseline. Walk-forward is mixed (5/11 windows positive), with 2021-2024 windows mostly negative and only the most recent 2025-2026 windows turning modestly positive, suggesting the prior edge was a small recent-regime effect rather than a robust persistent signal.

5yr aggregate t5_net dropped from 1.62% (Loop-10 2yr) to 1.20% as older 2021-2022 windows diluted the recent strong performance, but the effect remains highly robust with 10/11 walk-forward windows positive and consistent across both markets. Realistic execution (0.16%) is barely above breakeven after costs/slippage, confirming the edge exists in idealized terms but is fragile after real-world frictions.

5yr aggregate t5_net (1.23%) is ~3x weaker than the Loop-10 2yr baseline (3.94%) and realistic drops to just +0.23%, but 7/10 walk-forward windows are positive with strongly accelerating recent performance (Jan25 +7.67% PF 3.57, Jul25 +4.51%, Jan26 +4.96% PF 2.27). KOSPI subset is notably cleaner (PF 2.25, 61% win) suggesting the edge concentrates in larger-cap bonus-issue announcements.

5-year aggregate t5_net mean rose to +0.40% (realistic +0.25%) vs Loop-10 baseline of +0.25%/+0.18%, with 6 of 11 walk-forward windows positive but median still negative (-1.00%) and low win rate (38.7%). Strong market split persists: KOSDAQ positive (+0.93%, PF 1.20) while KOSPI is negative (-0.53%, PF 0.84), so any edge is concentrated in KOSDAQ names.

Idealized t5_net dropped from Loop-10's 0.85% to 0.63% on the 5yr sample (n=4175), and once realistic execution costs are applied the mean collapses to -0.02% with PF 0.99, confirming Loop-10's negative read after costs. Walk-forward is choppy (7/11 windows positive but the most recent Jan26 window is -1.15%), and the headline edge is concentrated in a small KOSPI subset (n=304, +3.70%) while the dominant KOSDAQ pool (n=3871) only nets +0.39% gross.

On the 5yr dataset (n=2570), the idealized t5_net loss shrank from -2.62% (Loop-10 2yr) to -1.18%, and realistic execution turns essentially flat (+0.05%, PF 1.01), so the prior negative edge is not robust. Walk-forward is highly unstable (4/11 windows positive, including extreme +10.6% in Jul23-Dec23 and -5.7% in Jul22-Dec22), confirming the analyzer's neutral verdict.

The negative edge persists on the 5-year sample (n=1858, t5_net -1.22%, realistic -1.09%, PF 0.75) but is roughly half the magnitude of the Loop-10 2-year baseline (-2.38%), with 8 of 10 walk-forward windows negative and effect strongest in 2H23/2H24/2H25/1H26. Both KOSPI and KOSDAQ remain negative with PF below 0.80, confirming a robust short-bias/avoidance signal rather than a tradeable long.

verifications.reason: Scale-robustness evidence clearly supports "neutral". The 2yr Loop-10 baseline (+0.39% t5_net, positive_noisy) reversed sign at 2.5x sample size on 5yr data (n=8585): aggregate t5_net -0.11%, realistic -0.29%, PF 0.96, win rate 42%. Sharpe-ish flipped from positive to -0.011 (idealized) / -0.035 (realistic) — not just shrinkage but complete sign reversal, a strong regression-to-mean signal. Walk-forward shows only 5/11 windows positive, with positive contribution concentrated in 2025-2026 (recent regime) while 6 of 7 windows in 2021-2024 are negative, confirming the prior edge was a recent-regime artifact rather than a persistent signal. KOSPI/KOSDAQ split is unconvincing (+0.07% vs -0.30%). Neutral is a reasonable, arguably generous read; the data does not support a positive edge at scale.

Through the execution_realism lens, the neutral verdict holds. The realistic T+1 close entry mean of -0.292% sits well within the neutral zone: it fails the +0.30% threshold required to call this tradable-positive (it is actually negative), and it also fails the -0.50% threshold required to call it a useful blacklist-negative. Compared to the aggregate t5_net mean of -0.11%, realistic execution degrades returns by an additional ~18bps, which is the expected direction (execution slippage erodes any apparent edge) and confirms there is no robust signal to exploit. The reversal from the Loop-10 2yr positive_noisy baseline (+0.39% -> -0.29% realistic) on a much larger n=8585 sample, combined with mixed walk-forward (5/11 windows positive) and weak PF (0.96), supports the analyst's claim that the prior edge was a small recent-regime artifact rather than a persistent tradable signal. Through the regime_consistency lens, the verdict of "neutral" is well-supported. Across 11 walk-forward windows, only 5/11 (~45%) are positive and 6/11 (~55%) are negative — neither side meets the thresholds for a directional "robust" call (positive_robust needs >=60% positive; negative_robust needs >=80% negative). The analyst explicitly notes regime clustering: 2021-2024 windows are mostly negative while only the most recent 2025-2026 windows flip modestly positive, which is a textbook regime-dependent pattern and exactly the kind of high cross-window variance that should downgrade any directional verdict. Aggregate stats reinforce this middle ground (mean -0.11%, PF 0.96, winrate 42%, realistic -0.29%) — small magnitudes, PF near 1.0, and a KOSPI/KOSDAQ split (+0.07% vs -0.30%) with neither leg strongly negative. The signal is too weak and too regime-dependent to call negative_robust, but the reversal from the 2yr +0.39% baseline plus the clustered weakness rules out any positive call, leaving "neutral" as the appropriate conclusion. Confidence is held at 0.78 rather than higher because the slight recent-regime upturn introduces some asymmetry the analyst could have weighted differently.

Through the scale_robustness lens, the verdict "positive_robust" largely holds. As n grows from 2093 (2yr) to 4801 (5yr), the idealized t5_net mean modestly weakens (1.62% -> 1.20%, ~26% decline) but does not collapse — well within the "stable, not >50% shrink" guardrail. The realistic t5_net mean of only 0.1572% is well below the +0.30% tradability threshold required for a positive verdict, and is actually weaker than the 2yr Loop-10 baseline realistic figure of 0.26% (which itself only earned a "positive_noisy" label). synthesis.final_picture: After scaling from 2 years to 5 years of data across all 7 disclosure categories and running 21 adversarial verifications (3 lenses each), the honest conclusion is that **nothing is tradable long after realistic execution costs**. Buyback is the strongest positive candidate and its idealized edge (10/11 walk-forward windows positive, PF 1.62, both markets robust) survived scale_robustness and regime_consistency lenses — but the execution_realism lens explicitly refuted positive_robust because the realistic mean (+0.16%) sits below the +0.30% tradability threshold, exactly the friction-driven collapse the analyst conceded. Bonus_issue, supply_contract, and convertible_bond all weakened or reversed on the larger sample, confirming they were small-sample/recent-regime artifacts. The post-Loop-12-iter2 blacklist now contains exactly one category — **shareholder_change** — which is well-supported: all 3 lenses hold, realistic mean -1.09% is more than 2x the blacklist threshold, 8/10 walk-forward windows are negative with the most recent four half-years all strongly negative, and both KOSPI and KOSDAQ show PF<0.80. Halt_resumption's removal in Loop-12 iter2 is vindicated by this meta-analysis (realistic +0.05%, PF 1.01).
synthesis.methodology_note: The 5-year re-test was the single most valuable methodological exercise in the project so far. It demonstrated that the 2-year Loop-10 baseline systematically overstated edges: bonus_issue shrank ~8x on realistic execution, supply_contract reversed sign entirely, halt_resumption's negative edge dissolved, and even buyback (the most robust survivor) weakened to sub-threshold. The pattern is consistent — apparent edges concentrated in recent regimes (especially 2025-2026) did not generalize backward, which is the textbook signature of recency bias and noise mining. Three procedural lessons: (1) any single-period backtest, no matter how large the per-period n, must be cross-checked against walk-forward windows spanning multiple regimes before any verdict is trusted; (2) the gap between idealized t5_net and realistic T+1-close execution is the single biggest determinant of tradability, and verdicts framed only on idealized numbers are misleading; (3) the adversarial 3-lens framework (scale, execution, regime) caught the buyback overstatement that an idealized-only analysis would have shipped — it should be the default gate for any future verdict.
synthesis.project_status: Substantially answered in the negative direction across the seven tested categories; the first-version research goal of Phases 0-4 is functionally complete and the next phase should be sub-segmentation and new event types rather than deploying any current category to paper trading.
synthesis.pdf_summary: The 5-year meta-analysis across seven Korean disclosure categories (n=28,728 events) and 21 adversarial verifications found no category that is tradable long after realistic T+1-close execution costs — every positive candidate either reversed (supply_contract), weakened below the +0.30% threshold (buyback at +0.16%, bonus_issue at +0.23%), or proved regime-dependent. Buyback retained the most robust idealized edge (10/11 walk-forward windows positive, both markets PF>1.5) but the execution_realism lens explicitly refuted its positive_robust label because realistic returns are barely above breakeven. The blacklist after Loop-12 iter2 narrowed to a single well-supported entry, shareholder_change, where all three lenses hold (realistic -1.09%, 8/10 walk-forward windows negative, both markets PF<0.80, and the four most recent half-years all strongly negative). The headline lesson for methodology is that 2-year baselines systematically overstated edges and that the idealized-vs-realistic execution gap is the single biggest determinant of true tradability — the 3-lens adversarial framework should gate all future verdicts. Next steps should focus on sub-segmentation of the remaining idealized survivors (KOSPI-only buyback, size- or LLM-confidence-filtered bonus_issue), expansion to un-tested event types (earnings, M&A), and faster-than-T+1 execution paths before any paper- or live-trading deployment.
